answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a stake-and-reputation prism: each agent must lock a saffron bond before offering services, and its past performance is publicly refracted into a trust score, like light through a prism separating honest history from noise. Attackers spawning thousands of cheap identities pay the bond per identity, so a sparrow-sized fake costs the same as a real one. Honest agents earn the bond back with interest, while caught Sybils forfeit it, making mass fakery unprofitable.
